text: LR/Δ exceptions: do NOT assume maximum Δ or lr3e-3 is always safe. MSE RMSprop lr≥1e-3: versus ≥3× smaller Δ, wins22/36 corpus (better MLP6/6, equal12/22, worse4/8); at equal lr prefer Adam (RMSprop3e-3 loses33/35). Univariate lower-RMSprop-rate preference can occur even below this ceiling (K1063). Bigram optima depend on model width (K1071); wide multilayer univariate high-Δ fitting risk is comparative, not automatic last place (K1072). Tabular optimum changes with epochs/data rule (K1073). Short-budget XOR/spiral often benefit from high rates, but T2048 winners q_46d72e/q_fb4a7f refute blanket long-budget safety; no general replacement ceiling is validated.
mechanism: RMSprop's first steps are lr/sqrt(small square-avg) ≈ up to 10× lr with no momentum smoothing; in unnormalized MLPs these kicks inflate hidden activations and the MSE output, so training oscillates. LayerNorm bounds hidden scale (and residual paths keep the function near-identity), absorbing the kicks — predicts instability only when the RMSprop net lacks LN/residual, as observed (6/6 vs 4/8).
